draft_context.source_title: I’ve spent months with the Honor Magic V6, and no other foldable can touch it for durability or battery life
draft_context.description: Honor Magic V6 review: Two-minute review Chinese phone giant Honor has been on a bit of a roll recently. In 2026, it’s already given us the exceptional Honor MagicPad 4 and the compelling Honor Magic 8 Pro flagship, not to mention the impressive (albeit slightly pricey) Honor 600 Pro . Its latest foldable, the Honor Magic V6, keeps up this formidable streak and is easily worthy of being considered one of the best foldable phones today. The big draw here is the Magic V6's market-leading durability. I’ve taken plenty of foldables for a spin, from the clamshell Motorola Razr Plus to the tablet-style Oppo Find N5 , but I’ve always maintained that I would never actually buy one. Why? Because these devices are often simply too fragile. I’m pretty clumsy with my phones and regularly use (and I must admit, sometimes drop) them in the shower or bath, and there’s no way that I’m going to splash out on a premium foldable only to see it turned into a damp paperweight. The Honor Magic V6 is the first foldable I’ve tested that truly bucks that trend. (Image credit: Future) In its review documentation, Honor recommended not to baby the phone — I was encouraged to take it out and about without a case, use it in the rain, and so on. I’ve been doing exactly that and, after multiple months of use, it still looks brand new. With its IP68 and IP69 ratings, it offers the highest level of water protection that I can find on the market right now, comparable to most regular high-end flagships. Its fold is smooth, quiet, and, after being unfolded multiple times a day for weeks, is still as good as new. Honor says that the inner screen is layered with tough UTG flexible glass and has an SGS Imperceptible Crease Certification, and it really shows. The fold is near-invisible head-on, and only really shows if you hold the phone at very specific angles. This is the first foldable I’ve used where you can truly forget that it’s even there. All of this is underpinned by a premium design that’s impressively slim. The folded phone is about as thick as an iPhone 17 Pro Max, so it feels great in the hands. Unfolded, it becomes just 4.00mm — the same incredible slimness that we loved with the previous Honor Magic V5 . On that note, it’s a shame that Honor hasn’t really changed the design that much for this new iteration, though. The look is practically identical and, on a more serious note, the V5 often ran hot, and that’s still an issue this time around. It’s especially apparent when you’re putting the top-end Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 SoC through its paces, so be prepared for some thermal throttling if you’re spending hours in the most demanding games. Despite these minor shortcomings, the Magic V6 is a winner and another impressive showing for Honor. I’m eager to see what the company has planned next. Honor Magic V6 review: Price and availability Priced at £1,999.99 / AU$2,999 (around $2,700) Already discounted by £500 thanks to a voucher Available in the UK and Australia, but not the US The Honor Magic V6 is priced at £1,999.99 (AU$2,999), which is a pretty hefty sum, but roughly in line with competing devices like the $2,099.99 / £1,899 / AU$2,999 Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra . Honor gains a major edge when you consider that the V6 offers 512GB of storage as standard (the Z Fold 8 Ultra starts at just 256GB) and factor in the brand’s frequent promotions and freebies. At the time of writing, for example, the phone is already £500 off on the official Honor website thanks to a voucher, and comes bundled with your choice of an Honor Pad 10 tablet, projector, or AI voice recorder in addition to some earbuds — you can’t really argue with the value there. Value score: 4 / 5 Honor Magic V6 review: Specs Here's a look at the Honor Magic V6's spec sheet: Dimensions 156.7mm x 74.5 mm x 8.75mm (folded) / 156.7mm x 145.6mm x 4.1mm (unfolded) Weight 219g Screen Inner: 7.95-inch 2352 x 2172 foldable OLED Outer: 6.52-inch 2420 x 1080 OLED Chipset Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 RAM 16GB Storage 512GB OS Honor MagicOS 10 (Android 16) Rear cameras 50MP ultra-wide, 50MP wide, 64MP telephoto lens (3x zoom) Front camera 20MP wide, 20MP wide Audio Stereo speakers with Honor Sound Battery 6,660mAh lithium polymer Charging 80W Honor SuperCharge, 66W Wireless Honor SuperCharge Colors Red, Gold, White, Black Honor Magic V6 review: Design (Image credit: Future) Very similar to the V5 Smoother, more premium hinge Still a large camera bump The design of the Honor Magic V6 is practically identical to that of the V5. It is incredibly thin when unfolded, coming in at just 4.1mm, with a durable aluminium chassis. The back material depends on your choice of colorway, with the Red version using vegan leather and the Gold, Black, and White featuring a smooth fibre composite. Whether you’re using it folded or unfolded, this is a very good-looking phone that feels great in the hands. I took it with me to Los Angeles on two business trips during my testing, and multiple people complimented the device completely unprompted and were eager to learn more about it — something that I can’t say has happened with any other mobile I’ve used. Like most Chinese flagships, the rear of the phone features a large octagonal camera bump which isn't going to be to everyone’s taste. I do quite like how it looks, though, and appreciate the subtle tactile texture on the ring around it. The bump is also a bit smaller than that of the Honor Magic 8 Pro, which means that it’s less likely to rest under your fingers and get covered in smudges. Although the aesthetic hasn’t changed, there have been some big improvements compared to the Honor Magic V5 when it comes to the hinge. It’s much quieter and smoother this time around, helping the phone feel more premium and sturdy. When opened, the phone’s inner display looks totally flat, and the crease is totally invisible in most situations. It only shows up at specific angles and when the screen is displaying lighter colors like grey or white. Honor keeps things refreshingly simple when it comes to buttons with the Magic V6. There’s a small volume rocker and a power button on the right-hand side, and that’s your lot. They’re well placed for one-handed operation and feel pleasantly clicky. My only real gripe is the fingerprint reader built into the power button, which sometimes feels unresponsive and requires a few attempts to successfully unlock. Design score: 4.5 / 5 Honor Magic V6 review: Display (Image credit: Future) Both screens are bright and attractive Crease is barely visible Comes with pre-applied screen protectors Both of the displays found on the Honor Magic V6 are excellent. The 6.52-inch OLED outer screen has a 2420 x 1080 resolution, with a fantastic 2,000 nits peak brightness (or up to an absurd 6,000 nits with HDR) that ensures that it stays visible in even the harshest lighting conditions. It uses Honor’s Anti-scratch NanoCrystal Shield coating, which is decently scratch-resistant and has managed to keep the screen pristine throughout my testing. It certainly helps that the outer screen also comes fitted with a screen protector out of the box, though I opted to remove it early on as it picked up a lot of marks very quickly. (The inner display also comes with a screen protector, though be warned that this is an integral part of the display that should not be removed by the user. It thankfully seems much more durable than the outer one). Despite the rectangular candy-bar shape of the folded phone, the outer screen uses rounded corners, presumably to give it symmetry with the inner one. That inner display is a 7.5-inch foldable OLED panel, surrounded by impressively thin plastic bezels. It’s almost as bright as the external one, with a 1,300-nit peak brightness (or up to 5,000 nits with HDR). It’s decently high resolution at 2352 x 2172 and doesn’t look noticeably less sharp than the external one in use, so you can transition between them seamlessly. Honor also deserves some credit for just how closely calibrated both of the displays are: they’re practically identical in terms of color and together just feel like a natural extension of the same panel. Both the inner and outer screens feature an adaptive 120Hz refresh rate, too (avoiding a jarring transition between different refresh rates when switching between the two), which is fantastic for smoothly scrolling apps and social media websites. Lastly, you absolutely don’t need to worry about an ugly crease spoiling your view with the Honor Magic V6. There is still a fold that you can feel if you really examine it with your fingers, but it’s practically invisible in regular use unless you hold your phone at specific side-on angles or look very closely on a totally blank screen. I’ve been folding and unfolding the phone constantly throughout my testing, and it hasn’t become more visible either, which is a great sign for long-term durability. Display score: 4 / 5 Honor Magic V6 review: Cameras (Image credit: Future) Good camera setup Not quite as strong as the Magic 8 Pro Plenty of software features The cameras of the Honor Magic V6 aren’t quite as strong as those of the Honor Magic 8 Pro , but they’re still very capable compared to the rest of the wider foldable category. The rear camera offers a three-lens setup, with a 50MP ultra-wide, 50MP wide, and 64MP telephoto lens. Photos are bright and poppy by default, which is great for capturing the mood of summer days, and they offer a good level of detail — even when dealing with busy scenes and foliage. The main sensor offers 3x optical zoom, which works fantastically, alongside a much less consistent 100x digital zoom. This setup performs well in low-light conditions and those with challenging lighting setups, like concerts with bright strobe effects. There are plenty of software features to try out on the Magic V6, including AI-powered color filters and different photo watermarks. The ability to display the photo that you’re taking on the front screen is also brilliant for group settings. Both the front and inner display have the same 20MP wide sensor, which does a good job with selfies, even if the results are a little overprocessed. The Honor Magic V6 also has strong video shooting capabilities and can capture 4K video at 60fps. As good as it all is, though, I do think the results are overall less impressive than the images I’ve taken with the Honor Magic 8 Pro and its 200MP main lens. Cameras score: 4 / 5 Honor Magic V6 review: Camera samples Dashiell Wood Dashiell Wood Dashiell Wood Dashiell Wood Dashiell Wood Dashiell Wood Dashiell Wood Honor Magic V6 review: Performance (Image credit: Future) Flagship chip Can run hot Good RAM and storage The Honor Magic V6 is powered by the flagship Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, the same chip found in the Honor Magic 8 Pro, Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra , Xiaomi 17 Ultra , and other high–end smartphones. With this SoC, it should come as no surprise that the performance of the Honor Magic V6 is incredibly strong across the board. In daily use, you’re not going to notice any hitches or slowdown when navigating system menus, browsers like Google Chrome or Firefox, and social media apps. It’s paired with 16GB of RAM, which is more than enough for serious multitasking. I normally rely on my phone for productivity tasks like note-taking, transcribing, and document editing while I’m out on business trips, and my flow was never broken by sudden reloads when flicking between multiple apps — even ones that I hadn’t opened for some time. Gaming performance is also excellent. It almost goes without saying that casual titles like Plants vs Zombies 3 or Warhammer Combat Cards - 40K (two games I must admit I’ve been spending an embarrassing amount of time playing recently) are totally flawless. More demanding titles, like my go-to Zenless Zone Zero , will run beautifully at the maximum settings preset as well. The Honor Magic V6 does have a problem with temperatures, though. Extended gaming sessions will cause the phone to heat up quite a bit, leading to eventual slowdown. I also found that it struggled massively during the recent UK heatwave, feeling red hot in my pocket and struggling to run even Google Maps smoothly in direct sunlight. Given the phone’s thinness, I think it’s reasonable that it runs hot at times — but if you want a dedicated gaming device, you would be better off looking outside the foldable market. Only one configuration of the Honor Magic V6 is available, offering 512GB of storage out of the box. It’s a bit of a shame that there’s no 1TB model for proper power users, but this 512GB capacity will be more than sufficient for the vast majority of buyers. I still have almost 300GB of free space after multiple months of use. The stereo speakers of the Honor Magic V6 are decent, but hardly going to blow your socks off. There’s more bass than you might expect given the phone’s slight profile, and they can get fairly loud. Just make sure that you run to the ‘Sound quality and effects’ menu in the settings app and disable the various effects that are, for some reason, enabled by default. They just make everything sound washed out. Performance score: 4 / 5 Honor Magic V6 review: Software (Image credit: Future) Transitions between screens seamlessly MagicOS 10 is still a winner Sleek, iOS-inspired design language I’m a big fan of MagicOS 10, Honor’s Android 16-based operating system. The design is certainly Apple-inspired, but as an ex-iPhone user, I find it both visually appealing and easy to use. It has a liquid-glass-like aesthetic, with sleek, semi-transparent menus and rounded buttons. You get all the visual flair of using an iPhone, but with all the additional customization options that you would expect from the Android ecosystem. New icon packs, themes, and a range of pre-set options can be selected from the in-built themes app. You can even disable the transparency effects throughout the OS if you want something that looks a bit more like traditional Android. Smart features, like an AI tool to recommend images that would be well-suited for your lock screen and AI-powered widgets that use context to suggest the app that you’re most likely to want to use, make daily operation smooth. Other AI software elements include the ability to generate or rephrase text and a surprisingly good translation feature. They’re not all winners though. The AI Settings Agent (which allows you to type or speak sentences like ‘Turn off Bluetooth’ in order to change key settings) is laughably useless, while the so-called AI Memories App is literally just a screenshot tool with the word AI slapped on it. But compared to other foldables that I have used, the Honor Magic V6 is by far the smoothest when transitioning between the two displays on the software front. You will get the odd moment where things freeze up, or apps fail to resize properly, but the vast majority of the time it works exactly as you would expect. I soon found that being able to seamlessly access the larger screen made it much easier to compose apps in Gmail, or edit documents in Google Drive. Software score: 4 / 5 Honor Magic V6 review: Battery (Image credit: Future) 6,660mAh lithium polymer cell Best in class battery life Easily lasts for more than a day The battery life of the Honor Magic V6 is superb. The 6,660mAh lithium polymer cell offers more than enough juice for a full day of use, even if you play graphically demanding games or stream video content. I use my phone constantly throughout the day and regularly go to bed with about 25% of juice left. With light use, you could easily stretch multiple days out of a single charge, particularly if you enable one of the power-saving modes. 6,660mAh is the largest battery capacity you will find across the entire foldable category, and it shows in real-world use. The Honor Magic V6 can comfortably outlast both the Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold and Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7 (we’re yet to test it against the new Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra), as well as traditional flagships like the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. Honor devices are already known for their serious battery chops, but cramming this much battery life into a device so thin and light is extremely impressive. Battery score: 5 / 5 Should you buy the Honor Magic V6? Honor Magic V6 scorecard Attributes Notes Rating Value The Honor Magic V6 isn’t cheap, but it does offer significantly better value than key competitors. 4/5 Design A sleek, stylish, and durable design with a smooth hinge. It’s great, but draws heavily on the winning formula of the Honor Magic V5. 4.5/5 Display The Honor Magic V6 offers two great screens which feel like a natural extension of each other. 4/5 Software Honor MagicOS 10 is a capable and attractive operating system that’s well optimized for foldables. 4/5 Camera A compelling camera setup, only lagging slightly behind regular flagships. 4/5 Performance Extremely fast and ready for gaming, but prone to overheating during extended play sessions. 4/5 Battery The Honor Magic V6 excels with leading battery life in the foldable category 5/5 Buy it if... You want a foldable with serious battery chops The Honor Magic V6 offers the best battery life in the entire foldable category. It’s the one to choose if you need serious battery performance. You want a great-looking phone The Honor Magic V6 doesn’t stray too far from the design of the Honor Magic V5, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing. It’s still a fantastic-looking phone. You need a durable foldable The Honor Magic V6 is incredibly durable for a foldable phone. It has some of the best water resistance on the market, and feels sturdy enough to last for years. Don't buy it if... You are a hardcore gamer The Honor Magic V6 has the technical specs for high-level gaming, but it often runs hot under heavy load, which does hamper performance. Consider a conventional flagship or a dedicated gaming phone if you want to play the latest and greatest titles for hours at a time. Honor Magic V6 review: Also consider Not so keen on the Honor Magic V6? Here are two alternatives to weigh up, one folding and one not. Honor Magic 8 Pro The Honor Magic 8 Pro is a fantastic alternative if you want a conventional flagship with similar specs in a non-folding format. It’s cheaper, but features a larger battery, better cameras, better cameras and faster charging among other upgrades. Read our full Honor Magic 8 Pro review Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold The Google Pixel 10 Fold also offers a strong level of water resistance and durability. It’s the alternative to go for if you would prefer something running a more vanilla version of Android. draft_context.source_title: Industry Leaders Unite in Open Secure AI Alliance for AI Safety and Security
draft_context.description: Open source software is a critical pillar of the global economy. It underpins cloud computing, financial services, manufacturing, telecommunications, government and internet services by making technology accessible and observable to communities of experts. Cybersecurity is among the top three beneficiaries of open source software. The Open Secure AI Alliance — building on the leadership of the Linux Foundation’ s Akrites initiative and OpenSSF community work — will work to remediate and disclose vulnerabilities using open technologies. Just as open source created a shared foundation for software, the United States and its partners now face a choice in AI security: whether the defenses that protect our infrastructure will sit inside a few opaque systems or be built on open models, harnesses and tools that any defender can study, adapt and deploy. The world needs both closed and open models . For cybersecurity, open models and open harnesses are essential because they democratize defensive capabilities, increase transparency for defenders, enable cyber defense while protecting data, and complement frontier closed models with customizable, localized controls. Open source enables massively distributed community-driven and self-controlled defense – with no single point of failure. Open models, like any powerful technology, can be misused — including through attempts to weaken safeguards or repurpose capabilities for cyber attacks — but those risks are not unique to open systems, and they must be managed wherever advanced AI is deployed. The recent Hugging Face security incident delivered a clear reminder: cyber defenders need open, frontier agentic systems for self-defense. When closed AI tools — unable to distinguish attackers from defenders — blocked essential forensic analysis, Hugging Face ran the open-weight GLM 5.2 model on its own infrastructure to analyze more than 17,000 actions and contain the intrusion. That incident showed a practical truth: when defenders cannot inspect, adapt and run advanced AI on their own infrastructure, their ability to respond is constrained at exactly the moment speed matters most. Companies and countries need open frontier defensive tools and techniques so critical industries can build security systems across a multi-vendor ecosystem and avoid single points of failure. That is the mission of the Open Secure AI Alliance: to ensure defenders everywhere have open, frontier tools they can trust and control. Leaders across cloud computing, cybersecurity, enterprise software, open source foundations and AI research — including NVIDIA, Adobe , Cadence , Capital One , Cisco , Cloudera , Cloudflare , Cognition , CrowdStrike , Databricks , Dell Technologies , DoorDash , Elastic , HPE , Hugging Face , IBM , LangChain, the Linux Foundation , Microsoft , NAVER , NetApp , Nous Research , OpenClaw, Palantir , Palo Alto Networks , Red Hat , Reflection AI, Salesforce , SAP, ServiceNow , Siemens, SK Telecom, Snowflake , SpacexAI , Synopsys , Thinking Machines Lab and TrendAI are inaugural partners in the Open Secure AI Alliance, a movement to develop and share open technologies, techniques and tools to safeguard software and agents in the age of AI. Some argue that open models are inherently less safe because they can be misused for cyberattacks or modified to remove guardrails. Those risks are real, but they do not disappear in closed systems, and simply keeping weights closed does not prevent determined attackers from seeking or exploiting powerful AI. The right response is not to deny defenders access to capable open systems. It is to pair openness with strong safeguards, clear rules against malicious misuse, rigorous evaluation and rapid remediation. In cybersecurity, the safer path is the one that gives more defenders the ability to test, verify and strengthen the systems on which society relies. Defenders need both frontier closed models and frontier open models, working together, so they can choose the right system for the job and ensure that transparency, adaptation and sovereign control are available wherever security demands them. Open Research Enhances Cybersecurity and AI Safety An AI agent isn’t just a language model. It is a complex system built from models, harnesses and guardrails. Real AI safety and security depend on the full agent stack — identity, permissions, harnesses, guardrails, logs and evaluation — not just on whether model weights are open or closed. Open harnesses and tools make those controls easier for many defenders to inspect, test and improve. NVIDIA is contributing open models, model weights, data and new agent harness research to the Open Secure AI Alliance to speed the development of new cybersecurity tools and techniques. The new open source NVIDIA Labs Object-Oriented Agent (NOOA) project is now available on GitHub to make advanced AI safety capabilities more accessible for agent harnesses. The NOOA research framework enables harnesses to better integrate with models to make agent behavior easier to test, trace, audit and govern. Across the Alliance, contributors are building an open defense stack for agents — from identity and isolation to safe model formats, multi-model scanning and secure coding workflows. HPE contributes to SPIFFE/SPIRE , which creates zero-trust identity framework standards and methods that can cryptographically verify AI agents and services to ensure only authorized workloads communicate and access enterprise resources. Hugging Face has offered Safetensors — a safe format to store AI model weights, providing transparency and guarantees of no remote code execution — to the PyTorch Foundation. IBM and Red Hat’s Lightwell extends security across the open source supply chain with digitally signed patches. Microsoft’s MDASH multi-model agentic scanning harness orchestrates specialized AI agents to discover, debate and prove exploitable bugs. SpaceXAI has open sourced the Grok Build terminal-based AI coding agent to promote trust, transparency and new capabilities, and plans to open source the weights of the Grok line of models to support the developer and research communities. A Call to Policymakers and Regulators As policymakers and regulators grapple with AI safety, it will be crucial to recognize open models, harnesses and security tooling as defensive assets, not liabilities, in AI and cybersecurity policy. Blanket restrictions on open frontier AI systems would weaken defensive capacity and risk concentrating power, dependence and vulnerability in a few closed providers. Companies and governments should invest in shared open infrastructure for AI defense — datasets, evaluation frameworks, attack simulators and red-teaming tools — much as past generations invested in open source software. The Future We Should Build The age of AI agents can be one of resilience and shared security. With the right choices, open secure AI systems can give defenders the tools they need, strengthen competition, extend technological leadership and ensure that the safety and security of this extraordinary technology are built in the open for everyone. That future will not be secured by assuming that secrecy alone is safety. It will be secured by building systems that are strong enough to withstand scrutiny, flexible enough to be improved and open enough to mobilize the full community of defenders. That future is worth building — and the Open Secure AI Alliance invites governments, industry and researchers to join in the work of defending the AI era together. Learn more or share interest in joining the Open Secure AI Alliance.

articles.title: CEO AWS Việt Nam: Điện toán đám mây Việt bùng nổ nhờ AI
articles.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) là nhà cung cấp dịch vụ điện toán đám mây có thị phần lớn nhất thế giới, theo hãng nghiên cứu Synergy Research. Tín hiệu từ VnExpress So Hoa cần được đặt vào bối cảnh trước: thời điểm xuất hiện, chi tiết đã có cơ sở và lý do nó đáng nằm trong dòng tin công nghệ hôm nay.
articles.dek: Điểm đáng chú ý: Tác động thực tế nằm ở workflow, chi phí, rủi ro hoặc quyết định mua/dùng; CEO AWS Việt Nam: Điện toán đám mây Việt bùng nổ nhờ AI nên được giải thích qua lăng kính đó trước khi kết luận rộng hơn.
articles.hook: Điều cần theo dõi: Câu hỏi tiếp theo là tín hiệu này có thành rollout bền vững, thay đổi giá trị sản phẩm, giới hạn đáng chú ý hay chỉ là một nhịp cập nhật ngắn.

sections.heading: Bối cảnh: điều gì vừa đổi
sections.body: Amazon Web Services (AWS) là nhà cung cấp dịch vụ điện toán đám mây có thị phần lớn nhất thế giới, theo hãng nghiên cứu Synergy Research. Công ty đang vận hành 38 Local Zone trên toàn cầu. Cuối tháng 6, họ đưa Local Zone tại Hà Nội vào vận hành, đánh dấu lần đầu hạ tầng đám mây do AWS trực tiếp quản lý hiện diện trong nước. Tín hiệu từ VnExpress So Hoa cần được đặt vào bối cảnh trước: thời điểm xuất hiện, chi tiết đã có cơ sở và lý do nó đáng nằm trong dòng tin công nghệ hôm nay. Phần này cần dựng lại thay đổi đã có cơ sở trước khi chuyển sang nhận định.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Trao đổi với VnExpress , ông Eric Yeo, Tổng giám đốc AWS Việt Nam, dẫn nghiên cứu của GlobalData rằng thị trường điện toán đám mây Việt Nam tăng trưởng gần 20% mỗi năm, thuộc nhóm nhanh nhất khu vực. Tác động thực tế nằm ở workflow, chi phí, rủi ro hoặc quyết định mua/dùng; CEO AWS Việt Nam: Điện toán đám mây Việt bùng nổ nhờ AI nên được giải thích qua lăng kính đó trước khi kết luận rộng hơn. Phần này cần nối câu chuyện với workflow, chi phí, bảo mật hoặc quyết định dùng/mua của người đọc.

sections.heading: Chi tiết cần kiểm chứng
sections.body: Ông cho hay, khoảng 65% doanh nghiệp trong nước có kế hoạch tăng đầu tư cho điện toán đám mây. "AI là chất xúc tác cho giai đoạn phát triển tiếp theo của thị trường điện toán đám mây Việt Nam", ông nói. Khác với trước đây khi AI chủ yếu được thử nghiệm, nhiều doanh nghiệp Việt bắt đầu đưa công nghệ này vào triển khai trên thực tế. Sự chuyển dịch đó kéo theo nhu cầu lớn hơn về năng lực xử lý dữ liệu, hạ tầng điện toán và khả năng mở rộng linh hoạt. Câu hỏi tiếp theo là tín hiệu này có thành rollout bền vững, thay đổi giá trị sản phẩm, giới hạn đáng chú ý hay chỉ là một nhịp cập nhật ngắn. Phần này chỉ giữ chi tiết có thể kiểm chứng và tránh lặp lại nguyên văn cách diễn đạt của nguồn.

sections.heading: Ai nên hành động hoặc chờ
sections.body: Ông cho rằng Việt Nam hội tụ ba điều kiện để thị trường điện toán đám mây bước sang giai đoạn phát triển mới. Đầu tiên là nhu cầu từ doanh nghiệp. Nhiều đơn vị muốn triển khai AI nhưng cần hạ tầng có thể xử lý dữ liệu theo thời gian thực, đồng thời đáp ứng yêu cầu lưu trữ dữ liệu trong nước. Với người đọc, khung hữu ích gồm bằng chứng hiện có, nhóm bị ảnh hưởng, rủi ro còn lại và điểm nên kiểm tra trước khi hành động. Phần này cần gọi đúng nhóm độc giả nên hành động ngay hoặc nên chờ thêm xác nhận.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Môi trường pháp lý về dữ liệu cũng ngày càng rõ ràng. Trong khi đó, nền kinh tế số Việt Nam tiếp tục tăng trưởng, tạo động lực cho doanh nghiệp đầu tư vào công nghệ. "Điều đó cho thấy thị trường đã sẵn sàng và nhu cầu có thực", ông nhận định. Những thay đổi này cũng là cơ sở để AWS quyết định đưa mô hình Local Zone vào vận hành tại Hà Nội. Một bài tốt cần tách rõ sự kiện từ nguồn, tác động với người đọc và câu hỏi theo dõi để không giống bản tóm tắt link rời. Phần này nên khép lại bằng tín hiệu cần kiểm tra tiếp, không tóm tắt lại cùng một ý.

paragraphs: Amazon Web Services (AWS) là nhà cung cấp dịch vụ điện toán đám mây có thị phần lớn nhất thế giới, theo hãng nghiên cứu Synergy Research. Trao đổi với VnExpress , ông Eric Yeo, Tổng giám đốc AWS Việt Nam, dẫn nghiên cứu của GlobalData rằng thị trường điện toán đám mây Việt Nam tăng trưởng gần 20% mỗi năm, thuộc nhóm nhanh nhất khu vực.

Ông cho rằng Việt Nam hội tụ ba điều kiện để thị trường điện toán đám mây bước sang giai đoạn phát triển mới. Đầu tiên là nhu cầu từ doanh nghiệp. Nhiều đơn vị muốn triển khai AI nhưng cần hạ tầng có thể xử lý dữ liệu theo thời gian thực, đồng thời đáp ứng yêu cầu lưu trữ dữ liệu trong nước.

Môi trường pháp lý về dữ liệu cũng ngày càng rõ ràng. Trong khi đó, nền kinh tế số Việt Nam tiếp tục tăng trưởng, tạo động lực cho doanh nghiệp đầu tư vào công nghệ. "Điều đó cho thấy thị trường đã sẵn sàng và nhu cầu có thực", ông nhận định. Những thay đổi này cũng là cơ sở để AWS quyết định đưa mô hình Local Zone vào vận hành tại Hà Nội.
Nhận định về tương lai, ông Eric Yeo cho rằng thị trường Việt Nam "tiềm năng lớn" do nhu cầu về dịch vụ điện toán đám mây và AI tại Đông Nam Á, đặc biệt là ở Việt Nam tăng nhanh.

sections.body: Theo ông, khó có giới hạn nào phù hợp mọi trường hợp. Với người tự lập, nhiều thời gian rảnh thì 60 phút là ít, nhưng với trẻ mải chơi, 60 phút vẫn là nhiều. Ông đánh giá mức 60 phút là hợp lý khi áp dụng diện rộng, phù hợp với tâm sinh lý và thời gian biểu của đa số trẻ em. Với người đọc, khung hữu ích gồm bằng chứng hiện có, nhóm bị ảnh hưởng, rủi ro còn lại và điểm nên kiểm tra trước khi hành động. Phần này cần gọi đúng nhóm độc giả nên hành động ngay hoặc nên chờ thêm xác nhận.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Dù đồng tình với quy định, ông Tuấn Anh cũng cho rằng không nên nhìn game theo hướng tiêu cực. "Rất cực đoan nếu cấm hoàn toàn như nhiều người đề xuất trên mạng xã hội", ông nhận định. Game không đơn thuần là một hình thức giải trí mà còn giúp trẻ tiếp cận công nghệ, góp phần tạo động lực, truyền cảm hứng để có thêm kỹ năng. Điều này đã được minh chứng khi trên thế giới, nhiều tỷ phú công nghệ trẻ, nhà làm game, lập trình viên giỏi xuất phát từ việc yêu thích chơi game. Một bài tốt cần tách rõ sự kiện từ nguồn, tác động với người đọc và câu hỏi theo dõi để không giống bản tóm tắt link rời. Phần này nên khép lại bằng tín hiệu cần kiểm tra tiếp, không tóm tắt lại cùng một ý.

draft_context.source_title: Đề xuất giới hạn trẻ chơi game 60 phút mỗi ngày được ủng hộ
draft_context.description: Đề xuất giảm thời gian chơi game mỗi ngày của người dưới 16 tuổi đang nhận được nhiều ý kiến đồng tình.
paragraphs: Dự thảo Nghị định mới về quản lý sử dụng Internet, trong đó siết thời gian chơi game của trẻ dưới 16 tuổi còn tối đa 60 phút, thay vì 180 phút mỗi ngày như Nghị định 147/2024, đồng thời bổ sung quy định về cảnh báo sức khỏe và phân loại game theo độ tuổi.

Chia sẻ với VnExpress , ông Chu Tuấn Anh, Giám đốc hệ thống đào tạo lập trình viên Aptech, đánh giá việc sửa đổi quy định cũ có nhiều điểm tích cực, cho thấy cơ quan chức năng theo dõi sát tình hình thực tế, lắng nghe dư luận và kịp thời điều chỉnh chính sách nhằm bảo vệ sức khỏe trẻ em.

"Mức giới hạn hiện tại với ba tiếng mỗi ngày quá nhiều, trong khi các em còn đi học trên lớp, học thêm, làm bài tập ở nhà. Nếu dành ba tiếng chơi game, trẻ sẽ không còn thời gian cho những việc khác", ông nói.

Theo ông, khó có giới hạn nào phù hợp mọi trường hợp. Với người tự lập, nhiều thời gian rảnh thì 60 phút là ít, nhưng với trẻ mải chơi, 60 phút vẫn là nhiều. Ông đánh giá mức 60 phút là hợp lý khi áp dụng diện rộng, phù hợp với tâm sinh lý và thời gian biểu của đa số trẻ em.

Dù đồng tình với quy định, ông Tuấn Anh cũng cho rằng không nên nhìn game theo hướng tiêu cực. "Rất cực đoan nếu cấm hoàn toàn như nhiều người đề xuất trên mạng xã hội", ông nhận định. Game không đơn thuần là một hình thức giải trí mà còn giúp trẻ tiếp cận công nghệ, góp phần tạo động lực, truyền cảm hứng để có thêm kỹ năng. Điều này đã được minh chứng khi trên thế giới, nhiều tỷ phú công nghệ trẻ, nhà làm game, lập trình viên giỏi xuất phát từ việc yêu thích chơi game.

Ông Lã Xuân Thắng, Giám đốc phát hành trò chơi trực tuyến VNG Games, đánh giá cao "quy định 60 phút" vì giúp hạn chế tác động tiêu cực của trò chơi điện tử, nhưng vẫn giữ được vai trò giải trí, giảm căng thẳng sau giờ học.
